answer: I'd like to talk about a wait that felt far longer than it really was. A time I had to wait anxiously was for the results of an important exam, which took several weeks to arrive. It was my HSC exam, the final exam at the end of college, and my university plans depended on it. That waiting period was genuinely [[agonising]], because so much depended on the outcome, and there was absolutely nothing I could do to change it. I waited about two months in total. Every day felt longer than the last, and I found myself constantly checking for updates. To distract myself, I tried to stay busy with hobbies and spending time with friends, which helped a little. I read a lot of novels, played cricket in the evenings and took long walks by the river with my father. Still, the [[suspense]] was always there, [[lurking]] in the back of my mind. I remember trying to prepare myself mentally for both possible outcomes, which was difficult. On the day they were published online, my whole family crowded round the computer with me. When the results finally came and turned out to be positive, the relief was [[immense]], and my mother immediately handed out sweets to the neighbours. What that experience taught me was how to cope with uncertainty, which is a genuinely useful skill. Honestly, learning to [[sit with that discomfort]] rather than let it consume me was invaluable. I now handle waiting far better than I used to, knowing that worrying rarely changes the result.

followUps.q: Are you usually a patient person?
followUps.answer: More than I used to be. I can wait calmly for most things now, but I still find traffic jams and slow internet surprisingly hard to tolerate, so there is room for improvement.

followUps.q: What do you usually do while waiting for something?
followUps.answer: I normally read. I always keep a book or an e-book on my phone, so if I am stuck waiting somewhere, the time passes far more pleasantly and I don't feel it is wasted.

note: Specified HSC results and how long he waited; added father walks and sweets; plain mark 'valuable' replaced by 'sit with that discomfort' and 'lurking'.
